{% raw %}
Alagos can keep your loot points: a **pool** belongs to your guild (or group), and every change to anyone's points is a line in its ledger -- earned for attendance, an officer's adjustment, loot bought. Nobody's balance is ever just typed in; it is always the sum of their lines, so it can be explained.

Set pools up under **💰 Loot pools** on the **Features & limits** tab of `/guild-settings show`. It needs **Manage loot**, which officers have. If your server has more than one group, choose the group first.

## Choosing a system

**➕ New pool** asks for a name and a system:

- **Traditional DKP**: points for attendance, spent on items.
- **Zero-Sum DKP**: an item's price is shared out among the others, so the points in the pool never change in total.
- **EPGP**: effort points (EP) for attendance, gear points (GP) for items; whoever has the highest EP ÷ GP has priority.
- **Soft reserve**: before the raid, everyone reserves an item; when it drops, those who reserved it roll for it.
- **Loot council**: members say they want an item and what for; the officers decide, and say why.
- **Wishlist priority**: everyone keeps a ranked list of the items they want; whoever ranks an item highest gets it first.

The points systems (the first three) are a paid feature: up to 3 per group on Premium. Soft reserve, loot council and wishlists are **free** and don't count. A group can have up to 10 active pools.

## Points for attendance

Press **✏️ Points per event** and list what each kind of event is worth, one a line, like `Raid: 10`. From then on, when an officer saves attendance with **Finish & Save**, everyone confirmed earns those points. If attendance is corrected later, the points follow: a player taken off loses them again, with a line saying "attendance changed".

## Settings

**⚙️ Settings** holds the system's own options:

- **Zero-Sum DKP**: who shares an item's price -- everyone present except the winner (the classic way), everyone present including the winner, or the whole active roster except the winner.
- **Spending** (DKP): fixed prices, open bids or sealed bids -- how members ask for an item on a loot post (below).
- **EPGP**: base GP (default 100) and weekly decay (default 10%).
- **Weekly decay** (any points system, off by default for DKP): a week after you switch it on, and every week after, everyone's points -- and GP in EPGP -- go down by that percentage. Each decay is a line in their history.
- **Points kept by**: **Alagos**, or **the in-game addon**. Choose the addon if your guild already keeps points in game: Alagos then only shows its numbers and never changes them, so nothing is counted twice.

## Loot posts: bidding and awarding

When something drops, press **🎁 Put up an item** on the pool's screen: the item's name, its price, the event it dropped in, and the channel (blank means the event's channel). Alagos posts it, and members ask for it on the post:

- **Fixed price**: members press **🙋 I want it**. The officers see them with the most points first.
- **Open bids**: members press **💰 Bid**. Every bid must beat the highest, and everyone sees the bids. A price you set is the minimum bid.
- **Sealed bids**: the same, but the post only says how many bids there are. Only officers see the amounts.
- **EPGP**: members press **🙋 I want it**; the officers see them by priority (EP ÷ GP).

Nobody can bid more points than they have. A member who has claimed several characters picks which one; **Withdraw** takes a bid back.

An officer presses **🏆 Award (officers)** on the post (or picks the item from the **Items** menu on the pool's screen) and chooses who gets it. In DKP they pay their bid (or the fixed price); in EPGP the item's GP is added to theirs. **✏️ Award to someone else** gives it to anyone at a price you type, for loot handed out without bids. **Close without awarding** ends it with nobody paying.

**Zero-Sum DKP** shares the price out: among everyone confirmed present at the event (with or without the winner, as the pool says), or the whole active roster except the winner. An item awarded during the raid is shared once attendance is saved with **Finish & Save**, and if attendance is corrected later, the shares follow. Odd cents go to the first few shares, so the points in the pool always add up.

Made a mistake? **Undo award** on the item gives the points back -- the winner's and every share -- as new lines in the history, and the post says the award was undone.

## Soft reserve

Press **📝 Open reserves** on the pool's screen and choose the event (one in the next seven days) and a channel (blank means the event's). Alagos posts the reserve list. Members press **📝 Reserve** and type the item they want -- one each, or up to three if you change it in **⚙️ Settings**. Capitals don't matter: "Ashkandi" and "ashkandi" are the same item. The post shows who reserved what. Reserves **lock when the event starts**, or earlier with **🔒 Lock (officers)**.

When an item drops, **🎁 Put up an item** for that event. If people reserved it, only they roll: they press **🎲 Roll**, or you press **🎲 Roll for the reservers** on the award screen and Alagos rolls for anyone who hasn't. Alagos rolls 1 to 100 and re-rolls a tie at the top. If nobody reserved it, anyone can roll. In **⚙️ Settings** choose whether **an officer confirms the highest roll** (the default) or **the highest roll wins at once**.

## Loot council

Put an item up and members press **🙋 I want it**, choosing **Main spec**, **Off spec** or **Minor upgrade**, with a note if they like. The post shows who asked; only the officers see what for and the notes, along with how many items each person received in the last 30 days. Every award **needs a reason**. The winner and everyone who asked can read it with **📜 Why?** on the post; nobody else can.

## Wishlists

Each member keeps a list of up to 10 items for the pool, the one they want most at the top: **📋 My wishlist** on the pool's board (post it with **📌 Post board**). When an item is put up, everyone with it on their list is listed, by how high they put it, then by who received the fewest items lately (the last 8 weeks; change it in **⚙️ Settings**). Someone without it on their list can still press **🙋 I want it**. Receiving an item takes it off their list.

## Tokens

Some games drop a token you exchange for the real piece -- LOTRO's Rift tokens, WoW's tier tokens. Tick **It's a token** when you put it up. A game that knows its tokens needs no tick: in WoW, an item named like **Gauntlets of the Cursed Protector** is a token by itself, and its post says which classes can use it. After the award, the winner (or an officer) presses **✏️ Piece taken** and types the piece, and it shows in their history.

## Adjusting points

**➕ Adjust points** adds or takes away points for one player, by their name on the roster. A reason is required (for example "on time bonus"); it is kept in their history with who made the change.

The pool's screen lists everyone's balance. **Archive** stops a pool earning anything new and keeps its ledger.

## The points board

**📌 Post board** puts a board in a channel. For a points pool it shows everyone's balance, highest first, kept up to date by the bot a few seconds after points change. If someone deletes it, the bot posts it again on its next restart. Its **📜 My points** button shows whoever presses it their own history, privately -- what they earned, for which event, and every adjustment with its reason. Nobody sees anyone else's details on the board.

For soft reserve, loot council and wishlists the board shows the latest loot handed out, and **📜 My loot** shows the presser what they received.

Officers see any player's history with **📜 A player's lines** (or **A player's loot**) on the pool's screen, and **💰 Loot** in the reports menu shows the points balances.

## Moving your points to Alagos

**📄 CSV → 📤 Export** gives everyone's balance as a file. **📥 Import** sets balances from a file -- for a guild bringing its points from another tool: a **name** column and a **points** column (**ep** and **gp** for EPGP). Names are matched to your roster, ignoring capitals; names not on the roster are listed and skipped, and nobody is added. You see a preview first; on **Confirm**, each balance becomes the file's, recorded as one "imported" line.
